audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers render an all-Zaahen level chart while packet.levelChart reads Skill / Locke / Locke / Zaahen / Skill / Zaahen / Skill — and the page's OWN prose agrees with the packet, not with the chart. whys[0] says level 1 is even farm, whys[1] says 'Level 2 is yours', whys[2] says 'Level 3 stays yours', whys[4] says 'Level 6 is even', whys[6] says 'Late settles to skill'. The chart contradicts the sentences printed next to it on all seven rows.
audit.why: 49.3% over 412 games is an even matchup, and every prose field on the page describes the packet's shape. The chart is the outlier. Rows are proposed as one atomic group across both layers, paired phases[N].side with win[N], with ratings moved to match.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Locke / Locke / Zaahen / Skill / Zaahen / Skill in both layers, ratings 5, 6.5, 6.5, 4, 5, 4, 5.

audit.why: The spike entries are unusually well shaped for this page — Lvl 2-3 Locke, Lvl 4-5 Zaahen, Lvl 6 coin-flip, 1st item Zaahen — and they match the packet chart. Cooldowns from the kit support them: his W is 14-12s, his E 10-8s, his R 110/95/80s. Four entries present.
audit.corrected: Windows kept; real numbers added to spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanical gaps. (a) His W is described as a drain ('W Ominous Return drain') in spikes[3], whys[5] and 'late'; Riot's text says W stabs in a direction and PULLS enemies toward him — no healing at all. His healing is on Q and R. (b) The W pull and the Q recast knockup are never mentioned, so the page never says how a melee champion catches a 425-range blink. (c) His E is a dash, which Purgatory's grounding denies, and his passive can REVIVE him at full Determination — decisive against an execute champion and absent from the page.
audit.why: A player told 'his W drains you' builds Grievous Wounds against the wrong button and never learns that the pull is what starts every fight. The revive matters more still: it means a landed execute does not always end him.
audit.corrected: W restated as an 850-range pull, healing attributed to Q and R, grounding named as the answer to his E dash, and the passive revive stated where it changes the ult decision.

audit.why: Grievous Wounds is genuinely correct here, just for the wrong reason on the page: Q and R both carry heal flags. Anti-heal added to the 'late' plan.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal tied to Q/R rather than to a non-existent W drain.

edits.after: At 4-5 he spikes: his W pull drags you in from 850 range and the E dash burst punishes your squishy frame.

edits.before: His spike: Q Darkin Glaive poke and E Golden Onslaught burst now reach your squishy frame - stop auto-trading, hold E as an escape, and never eat glaive chip with W half-committed.
edits.after: His spike: the W stab pulls you in from 850 range and his E dash follows on an 8-10s cooldown - stop auto-trading, hold E as an escape, and never get pulled with W half-committed.

edits.before: Ult chicken: your R Purgatory totem executes him if he over-commits, but his R Final Retribution locks your E reset if he catches you first - the side that baits the other ultimate wins.
edits.after: Ult chicken: Purgatory's grounding denies his E dash, so drop it as he steps up - but his passive revives him at full Determination, so a totem spent on the execute can kill nothing.

edits.after: On his first bruiser item his Q and R self-healing out-lasts your single burst window.

Late settles into a skill stalemate: your totem threshold executes any over-extension, but his passive revive can undo it, so buy Grievous Wounds, pick him off at range and never brawl.
